passage:
Avni had been hot and grizzly all morning and would not be put down. If her mother, Binita, so much as bent toward the cot, she wailed. So Binita carried her on one hip, offered small sips of water and kept up a slow, steady murmur. When it kept going into the afternoon and Binita's worry grew, she took her to the clinic.

The room smelled strange, and the doctor wore a white coat. Avni screamed and twisted away. Binita sat down, held her close on her lap and said, "The doctor will give you a small pinch. It might hurt a bit. I am right here." The doctor spoke softly and kept the needle out of sight until the last moment. Avni cried hard, then hiccupped and buried her face in Binita's neck.

A week later, well again, she tumbled off the low stool and scraped her knee on the balcony. Her father Raghav scooped her up. "Ouch, that hurt, didn't it?" He kissed the knee and hugged her, and did not say it was nothing. Avni sniffled, watched him for a moment and patted his hair.

qa.q: Where did Binita take Avni when the fever kept going?
qa.a: She took her to the clinic.

qa.q: How did Binita's way of holding Avni at the clinic connect to how Raghav responded after the fall?
qa.a: Binita held Avni close and told her about the small pinch, and Raghav kissed the knee and said it hurt, not that it was nothing. Avni cried, then calmed each time, so being held and told the truth showed her the hurt mattered.

qa.q: What was Avni feeling in the clinic when she screamed and twisted away?
qa.a: She was frightened by the strange room and the white coat, and she wanted to escape.

qa.q: What could a parent do beforehand to help a toddler who is scared of the doctor?
qa.a: They could stay close and hold the child, tell the truth in a simple way like a small pinch, and never mention the doctor as a threat.

grounding: A toddler is shown clinging while feverish, frightened of the doctor, and comforted by a kiss on a scrape, each time needing a close adult.
